title: Synthesis of Enones and Enals From Alkenes via Alkenyl Thianthrenium Salts
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Herein, we show the stereoselective conversion of alkenes into enones and enals. Alkenyl thianthrenium salts are used as a readily accessible pool of stereodefined alkenyl electrophiles that can be engaged in two types of carbonylative Pd‐catalyzed three‐component coupling reactions. Using alkyl zinc species generated in situ from alkyl iodides, enones can be accessed via a carbonylative Negishi coupling. In the presence of triethylsilane, enals can be generated via reductive carbonylation.

title: Frontispiece: Isolated Ir–Se Sites in Nickel Selenide for Glyoxal‐Mediated Ethylene Glycol Oxidation to Formate and PET Upcycling
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: Sustainable upcycling of polyethylene terephthalate to formate requires catalysts that selectively drive the electrochemical oxidation pathways of ethylene glycol. In Research Article e6834878, Myong Yong Choi and co-workers show that the Se-coordinated Ir sites in NiSe modulate the electronic structure of neighboring Ni sites, promoting surface reconstruction to active NiOOH. The resulting catalyst enables glyoxal-mediated oxidation of ethylene glycol to formate and efficient PET upcycling.

title: Reconfiguring Interfacial Electrochemical Potential for Boosting Sodium‐Ion Transport in Composite Solid Electrolytes
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Sluggish ion transport kinetics between the ceramic and polymer phases remain a key challenge in composite solid electrolytes (CSEs), primarily due to a severe interfacial barrier arising from their intrinsic physicochemical incompatibility. Herein, molecular design‐enabled electronic structure engineering is proposed to reconfigure the interfacial electrochemical environment at the Na

By grafting different functional trimethoxysilanes from a targeted library onto the ceramic surface, the effect of the interfacial electrochemical potential on Na‐ion transport is investigated, revealing a strong negative correlation with the ionic conductivity of CSEs. The CSE with the optimal grafting molecule (phenyltrimethoxysilane) reduces the potential mismatch by 87% and lowers the Na‐ion migration barrier, thereby boosting Na‐ion conductivity by two orders of magnitude. title: Photocatalytic 1,2‐Boron Migrative Alkene Homologation to Access 1,3‐Difunctionalized Alkenes
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    In contrast to well‐established methods for vicinal di‐functionalization of alkenes, remote di‐functionalization is much more challenging and has achieved limited success. Herein, we disclose a visible light photocatalytic boron‐directed alkene homologation with alkyl halides activated by a traceless
                    tert
                    ‐butylsulfonyl (Bus) leaving group. The reaction produces a myriad of 1,3‐difunctionalized alkenes under mild conditions with excellent functional group tolerance. β‐Elimination of the Bus group not only drives the contra‐thermodynamic 1,2‐boron migration, but also regenerates a C─C double bond, thus transforming the sulfone‐based alkyl halide into a vinylidene precursor, rather than a traditional alkyl source. The synthetic utility of this method is well demonstrated by gram‐scale synthesis, downstream transformations, and the formal total synthesis of 24‐fluoro‐25‐hydroxyvitamin D
                    3
                    analogues. This work represents a very rare example of one‐carbon homologation of ubiquitous alkenes, thus establishing a new strategic paradigm for chemical synthesis.

title: A Scalable Presodiation Strategy Enabling Dry‐Air‐Processable Hard Carbon Anodes for High Energy Sodium‐Ion Batteries
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Hard carbon (HC) anodes hold promise for sodium‐ion batteries but are plagued by low initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) stemming from irreversible sodium sequestration. Chemical presodiation offers a direct route to compensate this deficit, yet its translation to high‐loading electrodes is crippled by sluggish mass transport and air sensitivity of the sodiated product, a barrier to scalable manufacturing. Here, we break this impasse by synchronizing acoustic field enhanced transport with in situ interfacial engineering. Ultrasound‐driven microconvection and cavitation overcome diffusion limitations within thick electrodes, delivering ∼100% ICE within one minute, approximately twice as fast as conventional immersion. A five second quenching in sodium difluoro(oxalato)borate constructs a B/F‐rich hybrid interphase that not only passivates the highly reactive sodiated surface against dry‐air degradation, retaining >79% ICE after 6 h exposure, but also selfregulates subsequent solid‐electrolyte interphase evolution, suppressing impedance growth and stabilizing charge transfer kinetics. Practical pouch cells deliver 76% capacity retention over 700 cycles at 0.5 C/1 C and exhibit superior wide‐temperature adaptability from −40°C to 55°C. By resolving the coupled bottlenecks of kinetic inhomogeneity and environmental instability, this work establishes a scalable, dry‐air‐compatible presodiation paradigm that bridges the gap between laboratory innovation and industrial battery manufacturing.

source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Noncontact radiation monitoring in extreme environments is essential across scientific and industrial fields, driving the development of x‑ray scintillators. Conventional scintillators continue to suffer from inadequate exciton utilization, poor thermal stability, or limited processability. In this study, we propose a self‐confinement strategy to tailor energy routing for constructing superior thermal‐adaptive scintillators. Two lanthanide‐organic frameworks, ZJNU‐1006‐Ln and Ln‐BDC‐F, are rationally designed and synthesized. Compared with the free state of pure ligand or its quasi‐confinement state in Ln‐BDC‐F, ZJNU‐1006‐Ln exhibits a strong molecular self‐confinement state arising from compact ligand packing, thereby enhancing exciton utilization, suppressing nonradiative energy dissipation, and optimizing the energy routing. title: Topological Regioisomerism Enables Triplet–Triplet Energy‐Transfer for Reversible Dual Delayed Fluorescence–Phosphorescence Multicolor Afterglow

ABSTRACT

Reversible TADF/RTP modulation within a single host‐guest system is challenging, hindering advances in color‐ and lifetime‐tunable afterglow materials. To achieve this, we utilized regioisomerism as a structural topology control parameter in a host‐guest platform to modulate triplet‐triplet energy transfer (TTET), enabling the transition from exciplex TADF to dual TADF‐RTP afterglow. The optimized system exhibits TADF‐associated delayed emission with an intensity‐weighted apparent lifetime of 617 ms, along with persistent RTP and ∼6.5‐9.5 s afterglow. abstract: Efficient perovskite photovoltaics require durable interfaces compatible with scalable manufacturing. Solution-processable metal-oxo clusters combine robust inorganic frameworks with tunable organic components to enhance charge extraction and suppress ion migration. Complementary clusters stabilize both interfaces of the electron-transport layer, enabling a certified efficiency of 26.7% and improved operational stability. This modular strategy links molecular interface engineering with scalable coating, offering a pathway toward efficient, durable perovskite solar technologies.

Nuclear quadrupole resonance spectroscopy as an operando tool for mechanochemistry
abstract: Mechanochemistry is an expanding and generally green synthetic route, which is attracting more and more chemists in academia and industry. Yet, its applicability is often still limited by the lack of information on the mechanochemical processes. Therefore, to help elucidating reaction pathways in the solid state, we need to develop new real time monitoring techniques. Here we present an operando study of mechanochemical syntheses relying on Nuclear Quadrupole Resonance spectroscopy (NQR). Two mechanochemical syntheses were followed in operando (i.e., real-time in situ) mode by NQR, namely the formation of a halogen-bonded cocrystal and the preparation of a hybrid perovskite, demonstrating potential applications of this original technique, as well as its complementarity to more conventional operando methods used in ball-milling (BM). Lastly, we show that our NQR set-up can also be used in real-time to follow the temperature evolution, during a reaction, directly inside the milling jar. This method, BM-NQR, represents a promising functional alternative to NMR spectroscopy for the real-time monitoring of ball-milling syntheses.

Symmetry-breaking induced highly active Ni sites simultaneously trigger interfacial hydrogen-bond network reconstruction for efficient CO2 electroreduction in strong acidic media
abstract: Electrocatalytic CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR) in strong acidic media (pH ≤ 2) offers many unique advantages compared to alkaline electrolytes, but it still remains some significant challenges including the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), low selectivity and poor stability. Herein, we report that symmetry-breaking induced highly active Ni sites incorporated within ultrathin covalent organic polymer nanosheets (p-Ni1/2Pc), can simultaneously trigger interfacial hydrogen-bond network reconstruction for efficient acidic CO2RR. Direct visualization via scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) reveals the presence of Ni vacancies and uncoordinated pyrrolic N, which collectively break the local symmetry around Ni sites. This asymmetry not only optimizes the electronic structure of Ni sites to kinetically favor CO2RR over HER, but more importantly, it reconfigures the interfacial hydrogen-bond network via uncoordinated pyrrolic N. The reconstructed hydrogen-bond network effectively restricts proton transfer, while symmetry breaking creates a CO2-enriched local microenvironment. Consequently, p-Ni1/2Pc catalyst exhibits a remarkable 97.5% CO Faraday efficiency (FE) and a maximum 402.9 mA cm−2 partial current density (jCO) in strong acidic electrolytes (pH = 1), while maintaining stable operation for 85 h without salt precipitation. This work highlights the critical role of symmetry-breaking in simultaneously engineering active sites and interfacial microenvironments for robust CO2RR in acidic media.

title: Spontaneous N-formylation of amines with carbon monoxide in irradiated water
abstract: N-formyl amines are crucial synthetic intermediates, yet their production often relies on methods requiring precious metal catalysts, suffering from activation barrier or generating stoichiometric waste. Concurrently, the astrochemical origin of formamide, a prebiotic precursor, remains debated. Herein, we report a catalyst-free, radical-driven N-formylation strategy that addresses both challenges. Using only water as the solvent and X-ray or electron beam as the energy source, we achieve efficient coupling between carbon monoxide (CO) and amines under ambient conditions. Scaling up with a high-flux electron beam delivers a formamide production rate of 0.35 ± 0.01 mmol L−1 min−1, with favorable techno-economic analysis indicating industrial potential. The reaction proceeds via the in-situ generation of key radicals (•CHO from CO and •NR1R2 from amines) generated by species (eaq−, •H, •OH) produced during water radiolysis, followed by spontaneous C–N coupling. This method exhibits superior C–N coupling reactivity for most derivatives including electron-donating and electron-withdrawing group and achieves a notable radiation-chemical yield up to 4.6 × 10−7 mol J−1. Beyond synthesis, this work may offer mechanistic insights into the related radiation-driven prebiotic pathway, demonstrating that radiolysis of simple mixtures (H2O, CO, NH3) can efficiently yield formamide, thereby bridging green chemistry and astrochemistry.

title: Van der Waals-modulated integration strategy unlocks scalable fabrication of high-density organic electronic and optoelectronic devices
abstract: The advancement of organic electronics and optoelectronics fundamentally depends on the development of high-precision integration technologies. However, existing manufacturing approaches for organic semiconductors, particularly conventional photolithography and stencil lithography, are plagued by an intractable trade-off between integration density and device performance. Here we report a van der Waals (vdW)-modulated integration strategy that circumvents this long-standing bottleneck, enabling concurrent high-density and high-performance organic devices. By tailoring the surface chemistry of an ultrathin Parylene shadow mask, we precisely tune interfacial vdW interactions to orchestrate deterministic mask manipulation and high-fidelity patterning. Consequently, organic field-effect transistor (OFET) arrays achieve a device density of 2,500 transistors cm−2 with an average on-state current density of 1.20 μA μm−1, among the highest reported for integrated organic electronics. Furthermore, this strategy is extended to monolithic OFET-organic light-emitting diode (OLED) integration, yielding efficient light-emitting transistor arrays. This work establishes an integration route that preserves the organic semiconductor interface while avoiding direct photolithographic contact with the active layer, opening a route toward large-scale, multifunctional organic integrated systems.

title: Intelligent hydrovoltaic actuation with proactive ion regulation during solar desalination
abstract: Solar desalination offers a sustainable approach to freshwater generation, yet it is fundamentally limited by salt accumulation at evaporation interfaces. While common salt-rejecting strategies can mitigate macroscopic fouling, they fail to achieve real-time monitoring and active management of salts at the metastable stage. Local ion enrichment and associated pre-crystallization processes will degrade efficiency through increased mass-transfer resistance and vaporization enthalpy. Herein, we propose active salt management as a proactive system function and fabricate an intelligent dynamic evaporator (IDE) that integrates in-situ sensing, adaptive decision-making, and active regulation. The asymmetrically oxidized PPy/cotton is applied for real-time monitoring of ion concentration evolution within nanochannels via hydrovoltaic actuation. Coupled with deep learning algorithms, IDE dynamically correlates electrical outputs with salt enrichment states, enabling advanced intervention before critical accumulation. Dynamic solar tracking enables uniform interfacial evaporation and ion enrichment, elevating the stability of hydrovoltaic potential signals and the recognition precision (93.8%) of salt enrichment states. Overall, radiation-adaptive and self-cleaning IDE delivers an average daily freshwater production of 12.3 kg m−2 over 100 days. This work shifts salt management from static material design to intelligent adaptive control, providing a scalable framework for robust and sustainable water purification.

EpiPack: A computational framework for reference mapping and out-of-reference detection for single-cell ATAC-seq data with heterogeneous peak features
abstract: Despite substantial recent advances in query mapping and cell type or cell state discovery tools, their application to single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (scATAC-seq) data remains challenging. The heterogeneous nature of peak feature spaces across samples hinders the effectiveness of existing methods, while the absence of dedicated tools for detecting perturbed cell types and states in scATAC-seq data further limits the depth of downstream analyses. To address these limitations, we present EpiPack, an integrative computational toolkit that leverages heterogeneous transfer learning and graph-based modeling strategies to advance scATAC-seq analysis. At its core, the Peak Embedding Informed Variational Inference (PEIVI) framework within EpiPack enhances mappable reference construction, query mapping, and label transfer, demonstrating that leveraging heterogeneous features in scATAC-seq data outperforms methods relying solely on conventional homogeneous features. In addition, EpiPack’s global-local out-of-reference (OOR) detection framework achieves robust and efficient detection of perturbed cell types and states, extending the utility of scATAC-seq to disease and perturbation contexts. With its modular design and transferable pre-trained references, EpiPack can be readily applied to diverse analytical tasks and is available as a Python package at https://github.com/ZhangLabGT/EpiPack.

title: Deep strong light-matter coupling in 3D Kane fermions without Dicke criticality
abstract: Deep-strong light-matter coupling is a non-perturbative regime of quantum electrodynamics in which the interaction strength exceeds the frequencies of uncoupled light and matter excitations. Whether a Dicke superradiant phase transition can occur in electronic systems with linear energy-momentum dispersion remains controversial because of the apparent absence of a diamagnetic A2 term in their low-energy Hamiltonian. Here, we investigate Landau polaritons in a bulk mercury cadmium telluride film hosting Kane fermions coupled to a Fabry-Perot resonator. The ultralow cyclotron mass of Kane fermions and a thermally tunable carrier density enable tuning from weak to deep-strong coupling, reaching the single-mode coupling strength of 1.6 above room temperature. Near the Dirac point (100 K), deep-strong coupling coexists with linear low-energy dispersion. Our microscopic quantum theory and classical electromagnetic simulations are in agreement with measured spectra. We conclude that a diamagnetic A2 term emerges despite the linear dispersion, preventing a Dicke superradiant phase transition.

title: Precise Control of Spin–Orbit Coupling for High‐Efficiency Room‐Temperature Phosphorescence: Toward Photo‐Responsive Patterning and Visual Oxygen Sensing
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Photo‐responsive pure organic room‐temperature phosphorescence (RTP) materials rely on the compatible synergy between high phosphorescence quantum yield (
                    Φ
                    P
                    ) and high oxygen sensitivity. However, a fundamental dilemma exists: high
                    Φ
                    P
                    typically requires a shorter triplet exciton lifetime to suppress non‐radiative deactivation, whereas high oxygen sensitivity demands a longer triplet lifetime for efficient energy transfer. To resolve this contradiction, a series of pure organic RTP molecules are designed via the functional unit combination strategy. In these molecules, the flexible (4‐(tert‐butyl)phenyl)thio unit undergoes excited‐state geometric torsion, and the nonbonding n‐orbital of the sulfur atom is decoupled to varying degrees from the π‐orbital of the RTP core, enabling precise control of the spin‐orbit coupling (SOC) strength. Among them, the optimal molecule 56M2T achieves both a high oxygen sensitivity and a high
                    Φ
                    P
                    of 87.6%, exhibiting excellent photo‐responsive RTP enhancement. Based on this photo‐responsive dynamic RTP, we have further developed a high‐contrast, cyclically‐stable “optical writing & humidity erasing” photo‐responsive patterning system and a low‐cost time‐dependent method for visual oxygen sensing. This work not only provides novel insights into the molecular design of highly efficient and oxygen‐sensitive RTP materials, but also sheds light on their application in the field of intelligent responses.

title: Synthetic Pathway Modulation of Metal Organization in Multivariate Metal–Organic Frameworks
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Multivariate metal–organic frameworks (MTV MOFs) incorporate various metals and/or linkers within a periodic backbone, offering structural diversity and emergent functionalities. Typically, conventional one‐pot synthesis does not allow for any control over the spatial arrangement or sequencing of metals within the framework. Here, we present a synthetic strategy to alter metal arrangement in multimetallic MTV MOFs, yielding materials with nearly identical composition yet distinct properties. Using isostructural
                    
                      m
                      CB‐Co
                    
                    and
                    
                      m
                      CB‐Ni

High‐resolution electrospray ionization mass spectrometry (ESI‐HRMS) reveals the formation of distinct precursor species in solution, suggesting that prenucleation chemistry influences the final metal arrangement. This work establishes a new approach for modulating metal arrangement in MTV MOFs, enabling tunable functional properties in multimetallic frameworks for applications in catalysis, electronics, and quantum materials.

title: Mitochondria‐Inspired COF Nanochannels for Reversible Directional Ion Transport for Osmotic Power Generation
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Directional ion transport in artificial nanochannels usually relies on fixed structural or chemical asymmetry, which restricts adaptive regulation. Inspired by proton transport in mitochondrial ATP synthase, we fabricate pH‐responsive PAN‐supported COF nanochannel membranes via liquid–liquid confined interfacial polymerization. Transmembrane pH polarization triggers asymmetric charge regulation and builds an internal electric field. The membranes show pH‐dependent ion transport, with conductance spanning 0.4–1005.5 µS and a forward/reverse power density ratio of 202. Under a 100‐fold NaCl gradient and pH 1/13 polarization, they deliver 20.2 W m
                    −
                    2
                    . Experiments verify pH‐dependent COF charge regulation, while simulations indicate internal electric fields modulate ion migration together with diffusion. Salinity and pH gradients supply transport driving force; COF charge regulation dominates directional transport, and electrolyte properties, ion mobilities and electrochemical potentials tune current and output power. The observation of analogous directional transport across six chemically distinct membrane systems suggests the broader applicability of pH‐mediated transport regulation. These results provide insight into adaptive ion regulation and a strategy for energy conversion under combined salinity and pH gradients.

title: Synergistic Bimolecular Reconstruction of the Perovskite‐Carbon Interface Enables 23.6%‐Efficiency Fully Printable Mesoscopic Perovskite Solar Cells
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Hole‐conductor‐free, fully printable mesoscopic perovskite solar cells (p‐MPSCs) hold compelling promise for photovoltaic industrialization. However, their power conversion efficiency (PCE) remains constrained by limited hole collection at the perovskite‐carbon interface. Here, we introduce a synergistic bimolecular post‐treatment using toluene diisocyanate (TDI) and 4‐methyl sulfonyl phenyl methylammonium chloride (MSBH) to reconstruct this critical interface. We demonstrate that TDI reacts with surface formamidinium to polish and activate the perovskite terminations, while MSBH subsequently grafts onto this activated surface. This combined action simultaneously reconstructs the interface with optimized surface energy band bending and minimized interfacial defects, thereby facilitating hole extraction and suppressing non‐radiative recombination. Consequently, this strategy elevates the PCE of small‐area p‐MPSCs (0.1 cm
                    2
                    ) to 23.6%. Furthermore, it enables the fabrication of a p‐MPSC minimodule with an active area of 52.7 cm
                    2
                    , achieving a PCE of 22.1%, among the highest values ever reported for carbon‐based, fully printable architectures. Devices retained 98% of their initial PCE after 750 h of operational stability testing at 55°C ± 5°C. This work provides an effective interface reconstruction strategy that concurrently addresses defect passivation and energy alignment, paving the way for high‐performance, stable, and scalable cost‐effective perovskite photovoltaics.

title: Flexible 2D Donor‐Acceptor MOFs Enable Tunable and Pressure‐Responsive TSCT–TADF for Heterocrystal Photonic Logic
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Efficient thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) materials that combine high efficiency, color tunability, and dynamic stimulus responsiveness are highly desirable for adaptive photonic technologies, yet remain difficult to realize within a single crystalline platform. Here, flexible two‐dimensional (2D) donor‐acceptor (D–A) metal‐organic frameworks (MOFs) are developed through integrating an aggregation‐induced‐emission‐active triphenylamine donor with size‐matched electron‐deficient acceptors. Solvent‐directed assembly, donor conformational flexibility, and acceptor electronic modulation cooperatively regulate the D–A packing and through‐space charge‐transfer (TSCT) effect. The resulting MOFs exhibit broadly tunable TADF emission (474–635 nm), delayed lifetimes (0.11–7.65 µs), and photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQY, 0.52%–74.24%). Relative to the DMF‐derived structures, the DMA‐derived MOFs display increases of up to 51‐fold in delayed lifetime and 6‐fold in PLQY, while calculations support an unconventional high‐lying reverse intersystem crossing (hRISC) pathway. More importantly, the structural adaptability of the layered frameworks enables pressure‐induced reconfiguration of D–A interactions, giving rise to reversible piezochromic TSCT–TADF with emission shifts of up to 113 nm. A multicomponent heterocrystal is further constructed to translate pressure‐dependent emission changes into optical logic operations. These results establish flexible 2D D–A MOFs as a dynamic platform for integrating efficient TADF, mechanical responsiveness, and heterocrystal photonic functionality.

title: Reconceptualizing Thermal Runaway Mechanisms in Sulfide Solid‐State Batteries via Dynamic Interfacial Reconstruction
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The commercialization of sulfide‐based all‐solid‐state batteries (ASSBs) is often predicated on their perceived “intrinsic safety”. However, recent evidence of violent thermal runaway under abuse conditions has shattered this consensus, revealing a sobering gap in our mechanistic understanding of solid‐state failure. In this Perspective, we argue that the current stagnation in safety research stems from a “liquid‐legacy” mindset that fails to account for the unique solid–solid reactive landscape. We propose that the thermal failure of sulfide ASSBs is fundamentally governed by a dynamic interfacial reconstruction involving the continuous electrochemical and chemo‐mechanical evolution of the interphase during cycling. By deconstructing the staged thermochemical cascade, we demonstrate how cycling‐induced metastable species, such as polysulfides and mixed‐conducting interphases, act as reactive “pre‐conditioners” that dictate failure pathways. This framework explains long‐standing experimental inconsistencies, including divergent SO
                    2
                    evolution profiles and fluctuating trigger temperatures across identical material couples. This shift from a static material‐centric view to a dynamic interface‐centric framework reframes the rational design of truly robust, next‐generation energy storage systems.

ABSTRACT

DFT calculations suggest that the reconstructed interface involves the coexistence of net intercomponent charge redistribution and localized bond polarization, with residual carbon contributing to interfacial electronic coupling. title: Spatiotemporally Controlled Lithium Delivery via a Graphene‐Hydrogel System for Wnt Activation and Spinal Cord Repair
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Wnt signaling plays essential roles in neural development and has significant potential to promote regeneration after central nervous system (CNS) injury. However, therapeutic strategies that locally modulate Wnt signaling in vivo remain limited. Herein, we develop a battery‐inspired graphene‐lithium hydrogel (GLH) that enables sustained, controllable delivery of lithium ions (Li
                    +
                    ) to injury sites. Li
                    +
                    inhibits glycogen synthase kinase 3β (GSK3β), activating pro‐regenerative Wnt/β‐catenin signaling. Beyond Wnt activation, GLH provides complementary therapeutic functions: oxidation of lithium (0) attenuates reactive oxygen species‐associated stress, while the gelatin‐based hydrogel matrix supplies a permissive extracellular matrix (ECM)‐like niche. In co‐cultures of human‐induced pluripotent stem cell‐derived neural progenitor cells and macrophages, GLH suppresses pro‐inflammatory signaling and enhances neurogenesis. In a murine spinal cord injury complete transection model, a single GLH injection sustains Wnt activation for over one week, reduces acute neuroinflammation and astroglial/fibrotic scarring, and promotes long‐term tissue preservation and functional recovery. Transcriptomic and protein analyses further support coordinated modulation of Wnt‐related, redox, inflammatory, and ECM‐remodeling pathways, accompanying improved locomotor and bladder function and reduced neuropathic pain. Given the conserved role of Wnt signaling in regeneration, the GLH offers a multifunctional materials platform with potential applicability beyond the CNS.

title: Halide Perovskite Heterojunction Crossbar Arrays for Selector‐Free Analog In‐Memory Computing
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Passive memristor crossbars require each cell to suppress sneak‐path currents while retaining gradual, reproducible conductance programmability. In halide perovskites, however, sneak‐current suppression and analog programmability have rarely been integrated and validated across passive arrays. Fabricated arrays have typically relied on peripheral circuitry to mitigate parasitic currents, whereas self‐rectifying analog memristors have largely remained at the single‐device level. Here, a discrete three‐dimensional/two‐dimensional (3D/2D) FAPbI
                    3
                    /BDAPbI
                    4
                    heterojunction, formed through controlled in situ conversion, is shown to integrate diode‐like rectification and analog resistive switching within a single, nominally symmetric Au/perovskite/Au cell. The 3D perovskite enables field‐assisted ion migration, while the 2D perovskite introduces an interfacial barrier that induces asymmetric transport, resulting in intrinsic rectification and stable analog switching. A 32 × 32 passive crossbar array comprising 1024 cells, fabricated on silicon below 150°C, exhibits a 99.4% functional‐device yield, a synaptic nonlinearity of 0.007, and stable operation over 640 000 programming pulses. Cell‐resolved measurements demonstrate analog image programming and erasing, and a tiled‐array inference model incorporating the measured cell characteristics and electrical nonidealities connects the experimentally realized array to in‐memory‐computing performance. These results establish chemically defined perovskite heterojunctions as a low‐temperature, silicon‐compatible materials strategy for selector‐free analog in‐memory computing.

title: Ultrarobust and Thermo‐Mechano‐Photo‐Responsive Elastomers by Supramolecular and Dynamic 3D Topological Architectures
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Mechanically robust elastomers are being widely used in multi‐stimuli‐responsive systems including closed‐loop recycling, information encryption, and advanced photolithography. However, their advancement is hindered by an inherent trade‐off: structural integrity for mechanical robustness versus molecular‐level reversibility for stimuli responsiveness. In this study, we constructed ultrarobust recyclable and photo‐responsive supramolecular‐dynamic covalent networks (SDCN) based on molecular engineering of anthracene‐functionalized poly(urethane‐urea‐amide) (PUUA) networks with hindered urea motifs. Well‐designed SDCN achieves multiscale assembly through coordinated π–π stacking, hydrogen bonding, and dynamic covalent interactions, creating dynamic coupling between soft‐chain crosslinks and self‐assembly hard domains, and driving microphase separation. Under stretching, strain‐activated disassembly of dynamically assembled nanostructures synergizes with stress‐induced crystallization, in situ evolving three‐dimensional topological architectures and promoting strength‐toughness enhancement. Consequently, PUUA elastomers exhibit remarkable mechanical performance (100.17 MPa tensile strength, 1286.79% elongation and 498.15 MJ m
                    −3
                    toughness at room temperature; 113.67 MPa strength and 667.8% elongation at −40°C) and recycling performance (92.4% recyclability via solvent reprocessing). Significantly, UV‐responsive anthracene photonic moieties combined with temperature‐mediated interfacial SDCN transition enable fluorescent encryption and sub‐micron photolithographic patterning. Therefore, this work coordinates dynamic thermal‐mechanical‐optical responses and multi‐scale molecular transition mechanisms, which can be expected to boost high‐precision photolithographic patterning and flexible microcircuit printing fields.

title: 3D‐Printable Bioinspired Heterostructured Polymer With Exceptional Toughness and Fatigue Resistance
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Polymeric materials are widely used in load‐bearing biomedical applications, yet achieving concurrent high fracture toughness and fatigue resistance remains a longstanding challenge due to their intrinsic trade‐off. Here, we propose a bioinspired heterostructure (BIHS) fatigue‐resistant strategy inspired by the material‐structure synergy of natural intervertebral discs (IVDs). The optimized BIHS composite achieves a fracture toughness of 1252 ± 70.13 kJ/m
                    2
                    and a fatigue threshold of 8010 J/m
                    2
                    , outperforming conventional polymer materials. The BIHS enables stress redistribution at crack tips and activates multiple energy‐dissipation pathways, including crack bridging and deflection, fiber pull‐out and rupture, and interfacial interactions, thereby suppressing crack initiation and propagation under cyclic loading. Leveraging this design, we further develop a BIHS‐IVD that withstands 1.5 × 10
                    7
                    cycles without failure under physiological loading in saline conditions, corresponding to an estimated 45‐year cycle‐equivalent fatigue life. These results establish a generalizable bioinspired design framework for durable polymeric materials and provide a promising pathway toward long‐lasting biomedical implants.

title: Orthogonal Self‐Assembled Two‐Dimensional Charge‐Transfer Cocrystals With Superior Photothermal Stability for Low‐Loss NIR‐II Waveguiding and Epitaxial Heterostructure Fabrication
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Low‐dimensional organic near‐infrared (NIR) crystals hold tremendous potential for integrated photonics. However, simultaneously achieving two‐dimensional (2D) structural growth and low‐loss waveguiding within the NIR‐II region remains a formidable challenge due to one‐dimensional (1D) packing tendencies imposed by strong charge transfer (CT) interactions. In this study, we strategically choose the extended π‐conjugated structure donor dithieno[2,3‐d:2',3'‐d']benzo[1,2‐b:4,5‐b']dithiophene and the strong electron‐withdrawing acceptor tetracyanoquinodimethane, and report the first large‐scale preparation of 2D organic CT cocrystal microsheets with NIR‐II emission at 1050 nm via a gas‐phase self‐assembly. The strategically expanded conjugation framework not only further promotes the luminescence red‐shift but also introduces an interaction network with orthogonal directions, counterbalancing the intrinsic 1D stacking constraints brought by the strong CT interactions and guiding the crystals into a thermodynamically stable 2D morphology. The compact network plays a crucial role in endowing the material with exceptional structural and photothermal stability, as well as low‐loss optical waveguiding. Furthermore, attributed to the extremely low lattice‐mismatch rate, 1D‐2D branched heterostructures were constructed, which demonstrated efficient energy transfer (ET) and cross‐band optical signal conversion over 600 nm. This work breaks new ground in extending 2D organic cocrystals into the NIR‐II region and provides a promising material platform for low‐loss, and integrated NIR optoelectronic devices.

title: An Implantable In‐Tube System for Quantitative Precision Vagus Neuromodulation and Feedback of Intestinal Motility
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Electrical vagus neuromodulation of intestinal motility has demonstrated significant clinical utility in the field, where targeting the brain–gut axis can serve as an adjunct in treating intestinal diseases. However, quantitatively understanding vagus‐intestine interoceptive information about real‐time and in situ feedback on intestinal motility under the influence of electrical stimulation parameters is one of the most urgent challenges. Here we propose an implantable closed‐loop system that combines a scalable catheter‐type ionic piezoelectric (in‐tube) sensor as diverse as the gut, a microelectronic chip, an electrical vagus stimulation electrode, and a display interface to realize point‐of‐care precision vagus neuromodulation and feedback of intestinal motility. Owing to the radial gradient hydrogel structure design and stress concentration effect, the in‐tube sensor can simultaneously quantitatively detect and display four key parameters of intestinal motility, including intensity, frequency, duration, and local compression rate, with a high sensitivity of 7.0 mV mmHg
                    −1
                    and unique pressure–time integral behavior with a time sensitivity of 24.1 mV s
                    −1
                    , making up for the deficiency of traditional sensors that cannot obtain pressure duration. After implanting the in‐tube sensor in the anatomically challenging intestinal lumen of rabbits, we intuitively show how electrical vagus stimulation affects intestinal motility, which guides the optimal frequency window of 5 ∼ 10 Hz.

title: Ultra‐Strong, Leak‐Proof Bio‐Based Polyurethane Ionic Fibers for Sustainable Smart Wearables
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Artificial intelligence (AI)‐integrated digital flexible devices have been widely used in motion detection. However, the emphasis on sensitivity and response speed often overlooks environmental sustainability. Based on a green‐mechanical‐electrical synergistic design, a polar coordination and chemical confinement strategy is proposed to fabricate an ion‐conductive polyurethane fiber. Specifically, chemical confinement refers to the covalent incorporation of the polymerizable ionic‐liquid component into the polyurethane backbone through its hydroxyl‐functionalized imidazolium moiety. Polar coordination involves reversible Mg
                    2+
                    –carbonyl interactions that contribute to mechanical reinforcement and Mg
                    2+
                    retention. The resulting fiber exhibits a tensile strength of 52.75 MPa and an elongation at break of 1414%. Meanwhile, the in situ grafted ionic liquid provides an ionic conductivity of 0.209 mS cm
                    −1
                    . After 120 h of vigorous stirring in water, the Mg concentration in the test medium reached 1.9 ppm, showing limited Mg release under the tested condition. Integrating this fiber into smart fabrics enables full‐body motion monitoring and accurate recognition of complex movements with 100% accuracy. This study establishes a closed‐loop paradigm from sustainable molecular design to AI‐driven decision‐making, offering new material design insights for next‐generation green, safe, and high‐performance smart wearable devices.

title: Luminescent and Stable Eu(III) Complex Nanocrystals: A Class of Eu(III) Emitters Toward Amine/Ammonia
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Eu(III) complexes exhibit highly efficient luminescence, while their emissions are significantly sensitive to amine/ammonia‐induced quenching. Herein, we report a class of Eu(III) complex nanocrystals in which aliphatic amines serve as structural regulators to construct highly luminescent and stable ultrasmall Eu(III) emitters. The addition of aliphatic amines enables the originally insoluble complexes to be dissolved in
                    n
                    ‐hexane, producing Eu(III) complex nanocrystal solutions. The primary‐ and secondary‐amine based Eu(btfa)
                    3
                    PBI nanocrystal solutions showed photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs) reaching 24%–36% and 30%–37%, respectively. In a sharp contrast, the complex's luminescence was completely or substantially quenched when dissolved directly in primary or secondary amine liquids, with PLQYs decreasing to 0 or 0.0%–1.2%. The significantly suppressed quenching upon nanocrystal formation originated from the substantial reduction of vibrationally induced nonradiative decays, which was further supported by the low quenching constants toward amines. The nanocrystal's emission was further enhanced upon using the tertiary amines. A remarkable PLQY of 64% was obtained for tri‐
                    n
                    ‐decylamine based Eu(dbm)
                    3
                    dmbipy nanocrystals. The nanocrystal solutions exhibited excellent stability, with their PLQYs well retained after 10 h of ambient storage or continuous irradiation with 365 nm UV light. Furthermore, proof‐of‐concept experiments demonstrated the potential application of nanocrystal solids as amine/ammonia‐resistant warning labels.

title: Advancements in Multi‐Dimensional Hexagonal Boron Nitride‐Based Thermal Management Materials: A Review
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Hexagonal boron nitride (BN), due to its high thermal conductivity (TC), excellent electrical insulation, and low dielectric constant, has become an ideal filler for designing advanced thermal management materials (TMMs), effectively addressing thermal failure and electromagnetic leakage issues in advanced chips. BN structures in different dimensions (0D, 1D, and 2D) each have their own advantages, their interface morphology directly affects the TC of composite systems. However, there is still a lack of systematic understanding of phonon transport behavior at different interfaces in composite systems and their impact on thermal conduction network construction. This review focuses on dimensional classification and compares the intrinsic TC, phonon transport mechanisms, and network formation behavior of 0D, 1D, and 2D BN fillers. In addition to the traditional filler/polymer interfaces, this analysis also focused on the phonon transport properties at the homogeneous and heterogeneous nanoadditives interfaces of BN. At the same time, the TC of mono‐, di‐, and multi‐component nanoadditives systems were systematically evaluated, revealing the synergistic effects among BN of different dimensions. This review aims to provide a reference for reducing the thermal resistance of complex interfaces and promoting the practical application of micro–nano materials in the field of thermal management.

title: Engineering Tunable Helper Lipid Architecture to Improve Messenger RNA Lipid Nanoparticle Performance
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Helper lipids are essential structural components of lipid nanoparticles (LNPs), yet systematic design principles linking helper lipid architecture to messenger RNA (mRNA) delivery performance remain poorly defined. Here we identify helper lipid architecture as a major, largely unexplored design lever for optimizing LNP performance. Using a modular library of more than 80 rationally designed helper lipids, we show that systematic variation in headgroup chemistry, linker topology, and tail cardinality reshapes both LNP biophysical behavior and biological performance. Martini molecular dynamics (MD) simulations combined with multimodal structural analyses reveal that high‐performing scaffolds undergo a pH‐dependent transition into fusogenic inverse hexagonal‐like ordering, substantially lowering the energetic barrier for endosomal escape. These performance gains persist across the clinically relevant ALC‐0315 and DLin‐MC3‐DMA platforms, establishing helper lipid architecture as a transferable design parameter across distinct ionizable lipid chemistries. Translating these design principles into function, optimized helper lipid formulations restore hepatic protein expression in a mouse model of ornithine transcarbamylase (OTC) deficiency and increase antigen expression and immunogenicity in both preclinical models and in the in vitro human MIMIC platform. Together, these findings establish helper lipids as tunable molecular actuators of potency, tolerability, and stability, offering an engineering framework for next‐generation mRNA vaccines and therapeutics.
